classification.difficultyReason: The method and construction lines are supplied, but the hardest parts require using symmetry to infer triangle legs or reconstructing complete kite diagonals after finding their sections with Pythagoras.

content.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ theorem to calculate the missing length, then find the area.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle with a dashed diagonal, x on the bottom edge, 3 cm on the right edge and 5 cm on the diagonal.
spec.mathematics: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs x and 3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown x appear.

spec.description: Right triangle with horizontal base 5 m, vertical right side h and sloping hypotenuse 13 m.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown height is not completed.

spec.description: Upright diamond with perpendicular dashed diagonals, upper-right side 5 cm, right half-diagonal 3 cm and upper half-diagonal y. No equality ticks are added.
spec.mathematics: The intended rhombus has bisected diagonals. y² + 3² = 5²; the complete diagonals are 2y and 6 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither half-diagonal y nor the complete diagonal lengths are supplied.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=5^2-3^2\\y^2&=16\\y&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The complete diagonals are $2\times3=6\text{ cm}$ and $2\times4=8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{6\times8}{2}\\A&=24\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rhombus with one equality tick on every side, left side 17 cm, dashed perpendicular h and a marked 8 cm bottom-left segment.
spec.mathematics: The 8 cm label denotes the segment before the altitude foot. Each complete side is 17 cm; h² = 17² − 8².
spec.answerVisibility: The complete base is inferred from equality ticks, and h remains unknown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=17^2-8^2\\h^2&=225\\h&=15\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
All sides of the rhombus are equal, so its base is $17\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=17\times15\\A&=255\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Trapezium with vertical left edge, horizontal parallel sides 12 cm and 15 cm, right sloping side 5 cm and dashed perpendicular h.
spec.mathematics: The small right triangle has horizontal leg 15 − 12 cm and hypotenuse 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The 3 cm difference and the height are left for the student to calculate.

answer.worked:
The horizontal leg of the small right triangle is $15-12=3\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=5^2-3^2\\h^2&=16\\h&=4\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\A&=\frac{4(12+15)}{2}\\A&=54\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upright kite with perpendicular dashed diagonals, right half of the horizontal diagonal 8 cm, upper vertical segment a, lower segment b and right sides 10 cm and 17 cm.
spec.mathematics: The symmetry diagonal bisects the horizontal diagonal. a² = 10² − 8² and b² = 17² − 8²; complete diagonals are 16 cm and a + b.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown diagonal segments and complete diagonals are not completed.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=10^2-8^2\\a^2&=36\\a&=6\text{ cm}\\b^2&=17^2-8^2\\b^2&=225\\b&=15\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The complete diagonals are $2\times8=16\text{ cm}$ and $a+b=6+15=21\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{16\times21}{2}\\A&=168\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: Find the area of the semicircle in exact form.

spec.description: Unshaded semicircle with horizontal diameter d and an inscribed right triangle whose legs are 6 cm and 8 cm.
spec.mathematics: The right triangle gives d² = 6² + 8². The measured region is the semicircle, so its area is π(d/2)²/2.
spec.answerVisibility: The corrected area and diameter are confined to answer fields.

spec.description: Symmetric trapezium with parallel sides 10 m and 22 m, both sloping sides 10 m and two dashed perpendiculars with right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: Each outside base segment is (22 − 10)/2 = 6 m. h² = 10² − 6².
spec.answerVisibility: The outside base segments and height are not completed.

answer.worked:
The equal sloping sides give equal outside base segments, each $\frac{22-10}{2}=6\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=10^2-6^2\\h^2&=64\\h&=8\text{ m}\\A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\A&=\frac{8(10+22)}{2}\\A&=128\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle with sides 5 mm and 5 mm, horizontal base 8 mm and dashed altitude h.
spec.mathematics: The altitude bisects the base, giving a right triangle with base 4 mm and hypotenuse 5 mm.
spec.answerVisibility: The half-base and altitude are left for the student to determine.

answer.worked:
The altitude of the isosceles triangle bisects its base, so each half is $8\div2=4\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=5^2-4^2\\h^2&=9\\h&=3\text{ mm}\\A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{8\times3}{2}\\A&=12\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Square with bottom and right sides labelled x, dashed diagonal 10 cm and a bottom-right right-angle marker.
